chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
That he described tayammum: he struck the ground with his two hands, then raised them and shook them off, then wiped over his forehead and his two palms once.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu or ghusl under certain conditions
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the ground or earth used as the surface for tayammum
key_terms.بِيَدَيْهِ: with his two hands, indicating the limbs used to strike the earth
key_terms.جَبِينِهِ: his forehead, the part wiped in the act of tayammum
key_terms.كَفَّيْهِ: his two palms, which are wiped in this description
key_terms.مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً: one time, indicating a single wiping in this act

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed according to the hadith of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of performing tayammum as taught by Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. It outlines the practical steps: striking the earth with both hands, shaking them, and wiping the forehead and palms once, making it an important report in the fiqh of ritual purity.
